result.question: For our transformer fleet planning, take the known failure modes for a transformer and tell me which of them we can actually watch on Transformer 1 at site MAIN with the channels it reports today. For each failure mode, list the two or three most diagnostic sensors among hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati, il1, il2, il3 and inut. Then mark each mode as 'well covered', 'partially covered' or 'blind', based on whether those sensors have data in the available window. Only list sensors that genuinely discriminate that mode, not ones that just correlate generally. If a mode's key sensor exists but has no values in the window, count the mode as blind rather than covered, and suggest which offline test or extra sample would close the gap.
result.answer:
No further tool calls needed — the coverage scan gives everything required. Every one of the 20 channels you named has 5/5 non-null daily values on Transformer 1 (MAIN) in the available window **2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19**, so coverage status is decided by whether a genuinely discriminating channel exists, not by missing data.

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — failure-mode observability

| # | Failure mode | Most diagnostic sensors (from your list) | Why these discriminate | Data in window | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Partial Discharge in Oil | **hydrogen**, **methane**, acetylene | PD = H2-dominant with low CH4/H2 ratio (<0.1); near-zero C2H2 rules out arcing | 5/5 each | **Well covered** |
| 2 | Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating (T1/T2) | **ethylene**, **ethane**, oti | C2H4/C2H6 ratio sets the temperature class; oti confirms bulk-oil thermal driver | 5/5 each | **Well covered** |
| 3 | Thermal Fault — Core/Winding (T3, >700 °C) | **ethylene**, **co**, methane | C2H4 dominant with CH4 support = hot metal; CO rise means paper in the hot spot (winding vs. bare core) | 5/5 each | **Well covered** |
| 4 | Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking, D1) | **acetylene**, **hydrogen**, ethylene | C2H2 presence with C2H2/C2H4 in 1–3 band and high H2 | 5/5 each | **Well covered** |
| 5 | High-Energy Arcing (D2) | **acetylene**, **ethylene**, hydrogen | Same gases, but C2H2/C2H4 > ~3 with C2H4 also elevated separates D2 from D1 | 5/5 each | **Well covered** |
| 6 | Tap Changer Mechanical Wear | *none that discriminate* — il1/il2/il3, inut and acetylene are only indirect proxies | OLTC sits in a separate oil compartment; main-tank DGA and load current don't see contact wear or drive-mechanism issues | n/a | **Blind** |
| 7 | Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress | **dielectric_rigidity**, **interfacial_v**, oxygen | Breakdown voltage falls with water/particles; IFT falls with polar contaminants; O2 rise flags air/atmosphere ingress | 5/5 each | **Well covered** (note: `water_content` is also reported and should be added to this set) |
| 8 | Cellulose Insulation Ageing | **co2**, **co** | CO2/CO ratio (>10 = slow ageing, <3 = active paperfault) is the only online paper marker among the channels | 5/5 each | **Partially covered** — CO/CO2 indicate paper involvement but can't quantify remaining life or separate ageing from a paper-involved thermal fault |
| 9 | Oil Dielectric Degradation | **dielectric_rigidity**, **interfacial_v**, **dbds** | BDV and IFT measure dielectric strength/oxidation directly; DBDS flags corrosive-sulfur attack | 5/5 each | **Well covered** (`power_factor` is also reported and is a strong fourth channel) |

## Gap closers

- **Tap Changer Mechanical Wear (blind):** separate OLTC-compartment DGA sample (C2H2/H2 fingerprint of switching vs. abnormal contact wear), dynamic resistance measurement (DRM) across the tap range, drive-motor current signature during a tap operation, and a diverter-switch contact inspection at the next outage.
- **Cellulose Insulation Ageing (partial):** furanic-compound (2-FAL) oil test, and if the CO2/CO trend warrants, a degree-of-polymerisation (DP) test on a paper sample; adding methanol-in-oil as a routine marker would give earlier online sensitivity.

## Caveats for fleet planning

- The window is only **5 daily samples**; it's enough to establish coverage but not trends — ratio-based diagnoses (modes 1–5, 8) need a longer series before they're reliable.
- Side observation: the current DGA values on this unit (H2 ≈ 2,870 ppm, CH4 ≈ 7,330, C2H4 ≈ 16,600, C2H6 ≈ 5,460 ppm) are far above IEC 60599 typical limits, and `oti_a`/`oti_t` are both set. Coverage is good, but the readings themselves warrant an immediate DGA interpretation rather than just a monitoring plan.
